page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv6 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates balanced performance across most workloads. The instance achieves average ratings in stress-ng single-core (1948.58) and multi-core (7972.24) CPU tests, as well as an average Geekbench single-core score of 1975.0 and multi-core score of 7558.0. Text processing performance is strong, scoring 2658.0 in Geekbench. However, memory performance shows some variance; while small-block cached read bandwidth is average at 626.49 GB/sec, the PassMark memory score is weak, falling into the bottom 25% at 1436.15. Large-block uncached read and write bandwidths are 42.29 GB/sec and 28.08 GB/sec, respectively.

For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates strong text generation performance with small language models (135M parameters) at 302.13 tokens/sec, but performance drops to weak levels for larger models, such as 8.06 tokens/sec for 7B text generation. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 11.31 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 14.8 GB/sec. Given the high memory allocation relative to the 8 vCPUs, this server is configured for memory-intensive applications such as database operations, caching layers, and text processing, though users should note the lower PassMark memory score and lack of local storage.
